senses.gloss:
Cauṣaṭ Yoginī Temples
(‘temples of 64 yoginis’)
------------------------------------------
Yoginīs are minor goddesses, aspects of शक्ति or दुर्गा. They are often the gramadevatās or village deities supposed to protect the people of the village when propitiated, or, bring evil and disaster when offended. Their number is variously stated as 8, 60, 64 or even 65.
The चौषट् योगिनी तेम्प्लेस् are temples of that class where these deities are placed in niches on a circular or rectangular wall with a temple in the centre for the main deity.
Such temples, most of which were built between the 9th and 12th centuries, are found in Bheraghat near Jabalpur (Madhya Pradesh), Ranipur Jhorial near Patna (Bihar), Dudhati near Jhansi (Uttar Pradesh) and Khajuraho (Madhya Pradesh). The only temple outside Central India is found near Coimbatore in Tamil Nadu.
